note: HAL CMD's written answers to Sputnik India, 10 Oct 2026. MiGFlug 22 Jun 2026: 'brand-new Tejas Mk1A light fighters in Indian Air Force grey, radars fitted'. Radar software, missile integration and certification are still pending (TOI 18 Sep 2026: '90-95%'), so 'Ready on paper' can mislead; suggest 'Almost ready.' Add tag [HAL CMD | 2026].

note: New Indian Express, 7 Oct 2026. The Hindu 7 Oct 2026: the engine delay 'has, in turn, affected the aircraft delivery'. The last blockers for the first handover are radar, missile integration and certification (J018 covers this).

claim: India was building the Tejas at the same time as the Kaveri, both new (VO: Both from zero. That doubled the risk.)
source_quote: the Government sanctioned in August 1983 the development of a multi-role Light Combat Aircraft (LCA)
note: CAG 2010: LCA sanctioned Aug 1983, Kaveri Mar 1989, so both ran in parallel; GTRE had 'only a very limited experience of the GTX engine', and GTRE itself proposed proving the new LCA airframe 'with a proven engine first'. 'Both from zero' slightly overstates (GTRE had worked on the GTX-37 since 1982): optional 'Both almost from scratch.' 'Doubled the risk' is the narrator's analysis. Add tag [CAG | 2010].

claim: Kaveri target: 81 kN with afterburner (the 'heat and dust' phrase was dropped)
source_quote: Not one of the existing pool of prototypes however has been able to meet the 81 kN thrust target in reheat (afterburner) mode.
note: v2: J033 no longer mentions heat and dust; the 81 kN target is JE-023.

claim: A jet engine must go from idle to full power in seconds
source_quote: from not more than 15 percent of the rated takeoff power or thrust available to 95 percent rated takeoff power or thrust in not over 5 sec.
note: FAA rule 14 CFR 33.73 quoted in NASA/TM-2009-215668 (Nov 2009). This is the civil minimum; fighter engines must respond at least as fast. No tag on screen now; optional [NASA | FAA].

claim: A rocket carries its own oxygen; a jet engine must breathe air
source_quote: But unlike the rocket engine which must carry its oxygen for combustion, the turbine engine gets its oxygen from the surrounding air.
note: NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics.

claim: The high-pressure turbine blade sits right behind the combustion chamber in hot gas; it is the key part (on-screen: HIGH-PRESSURE TURBINE BLADE)
source_quote: the temperature of the gas flow behind the combustion chamber is 2,000°K (1,700°C), which is actually several hundred degrees hotter than the melting point of the blades.
note: Rolls-Royce, 2018. NASA Glenn: 'Leaving the burner, the hot exhaust is passed through the turbine.' RR 2012: 'The single crystal turbine blade is a critical component of the jet engine'. Add tag [NASA | ROLLS-ROYCE] to J052.

claim: So few countries can make these blades; the know-how was learned over decades
source_quote: Very few countries in the world such as USA, UK, France and Russia have the capability to design and manufacture such Single Crystal (SX) components.
note: PIB, 26 Apr 2021. PIB 10 Dec 2012 speaks of 'Tacit knowledge acquired by the DRDO scientists'. Add tag [PIB | 2021] to J068.

claim: The knowledge is a closely guarded secret; for decades no engine maker shared it with India
source_quote: Ministry further stated that no engine house was willing to part with their development experience for the benefit of GTRE as they viewed GTRE as a competitor.
note: 'Closely guarded' is supported (MoD to CAG, Jan 2009; Business Standard 2009: Rolls-Royce and GE 'declined to partner GTRE, apparently unwilling to part with cutting-edge technology'; Raksha Anirveda 2026: hot-section tech, crystal blades and source codes 'were never shared'). But 'Nobody sells it' is absolute and the film itself later shows Safran and Rolls-Royce offering full transfer with Indian IP (Snecma also offered joint development in 2001, per CAG). Fix J070: That knowledge is a closely guarded secret. For decades, no engine maker shared it with India. Tag [CAG 2010 | BUSINESS STANDARD 2009]. | v2: J070 rewritten to the checker's wording.

claim: The Kaveri years were not wasted; they built India's engine technology base
source_quote: Kaveri engine project has achieved higher Technology Readiness Level (TRL) in many critical technology domains and those technologies are being used in the various engine development programmes of the country.
note: PIB, MoD, 29 Nov 2021 (Rajya Sabha reply). Opinion line, fairly supported. Add tag [PIB | 2021].

claim: The gas, not the metal, is above the metal's melting point; cooling keeps the blade below it (J055, J067, J086 reworded)
source_quote: They are therefore cooled both internally and externally in order to keep them below the critical material temperature.
note: It is the gas, not the metal, that is above the melting point; cooling and coatings keep the metal below it (Cambridge: turbine entry about 1400 °C, metal 'in the vicinity of 930 °C'). J067 is fine as a recap once J055 is fixed. | v2: J055, J067 and J086 now say the gas is hotter than the metal's melting point.

source_quote: the stage burns for about 646s
